research.title: RealCompanion: Benchmarking Human Understanding from Reasoning over Longitudinal Real-World Conversations
research.why: Tests whether an AI companion that talks with someone for months actually remembers and understands them. Millions of people use chat assistants this way, so the question matters to general readers. It was the top HF Daily Papers item in the window (267 upvotes, featured 2026-10-05; arXiv submitted 2026-10-01, just before the window). Label it a preprint that is not yet peer-reviewed.

invention.title: SCM: local AI search for every photo and every frame of video on a Mac
invention.why: Open-source app that lets anyone search their own photo and video library in plain language, running locally. That makes it useful to ordinary readers and good for privacy. It had the strongest Show HN signal in the window (175 pts / 73 comments, 2026-10-04), and the primary source is the GitHub repo itself. Honest caveat: HN commenters raised frame-sampling and indexing cost, and it is Mac-only.

thread: Both the research and invention picks are about AI holding on to a person's own life (months of conversation in RealCompanion, years of photos in SCM), so the closing could ask what it takes for that memory to be accurate and stay under the user's control.
